subject: School Committee Candidates Forum
overview: Nine candidates for the Medford School Committee participated in a public forum to discuss their platforms and priorities. The candidates addressed questions regarding district budgeting, special education, and the proposed construction of a new high school.

items.title: Opening Statements
items.summary: The nine candidates introduced their professional backgrounds, personal ties to the district, and motivations for seeking office.

items.title: Round 1: Roles, Safety, and Infrastructure
items.summary: Candidates responded to randomly assigned questions regarding the distinction between committee and superintendent roles, school safety drills, mental health challenges, and the necessity of a new high school building.

items.title: Round 2: Operations, Contracts, and Equity
items.summary: Discussion focused on improving vocational programs, resolving teacher contract delays, and ensuring equitable support for special education and LGBTQ+ students.

items.title: Round 3: Curriculum, Funding, and Leadership Search
items.summary: The final round addressed the elimination of MCAS graduation requirements, potential federal funding cuts related to district policies, after-school programming, and criteria for the next permanent superintendent.

items.title: Closing Statements
items.summary: Candidates summarized their platforms, with a focus on data-driven results, community engagement, and fiscal transparency.
